stem: What is the central mechanism linking insulin resistance to hyperandrogenism in PCOS?
why_correct: Hyperinsulinemia directly stimulates theca-cell androgen production and lowers hepatic SHBG, raising free testosterone.
takeaway: Insulin → androgens → worse insulin resistance (a cycle).
discriminator: Explains why metabolic therapy helps reproductive symptoms.

D.why: Hyperinsulinemia directly stimulates theca-cell androgen production and lowers hepatic SHBG, raising free testosterone.

stem: Why does tamoxifen raise endometrial cancer risk while raloxifene largely does not?
why_correct: SERMs act as agonists in some tissues and antagonists in others; tamoxifen activates the endometrium, raloxifene is essentially neutral.
takeaway: Both: breast antagonist, bone agonist, VTE. Only tamoxifen: endometrium.
discriminator: Tissue-selective agonism, not a class effect.

A.why: SERMs act as agonists in some tissues and antagonists in others; tamoxifen activates the endometrium, raloxifene is essentially neutral.

stem: Which adverse effect is specific to long-term depot medroxyprogesterone (DMPA)?
why_correct: DMPA carries a boxed warning for loss of bone mineral density with prolonged use.
discriminator: Progestin-only methods also cause irregular bleeding early.
src: L11 S6; S9; S31; SG U6-R4

A.why: DMPA carries a boxed warning for loss of bone mineral density with prolonged use.

stem: Eight months into tamoxifen, a 55-year-old reports new vaginal bleeding. What should happen?

distractors.text: Add estrogen to stabilize the lining

why_correct: Tamoxifen’s endometrial agonism raises hyperplasia/cancer risk — new bleeding needs prompt evaluation.
discriminator: Raloxifene would not carry this risk.

C.text: Add estrogen to stabilize the lining

E.why: Tamoxifen’s endometrial agonism raises hyperplasia/cancer risk — new bleeding needs prompt evaluation.

stem: What distinguishes tamsulosin from doxazosin?
why_correct: Tamsulosin/silodosin are uroselective; doxazosin/terazosin lower BP more; all share orthostatic hypotension and a first-dose effect.
takeaway: Selectivity changes degree, not the class risk.
discriminator: Floppy iris syndrome in cataract surgery.

D.why: Tamsulosin/silodosin are uroselective; doxazosin/terazosin lower BP more; all share orthostatic hypotension and a first-dose effect.

stem: A woman with PCOS on spironolactone for hirsutism plans to conceive. Key counseling?

distractors.text: Continue; it is safe in pregnancy

why_correct: Spironolactone blocks the androgen receptor; avoid in pregnancy (feminization of a male fetus).
discriminator: Also hyperkalemia with ACEi/ARB or potassium.

A.text: Continue; it is safe in pregnancy

B.why: Spironolactone blocks the androgen receptor; avoid in pregnancy (feminization of a male fetus).

stem: Which adverse effect is most associated with sildenafil?
why_correct: PDE5 inhibitors cause headache, flushing, dyspepsia and visual disturbance (blue tinge, notably sildenafil).
discriminator: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors raise PDE5 inhibitor levels.

E.why: PDE5 inhibitors cause headache, flushing, dyspepsia and visual disturbance (blue tinge, notably sildenafil).

stem: A 79-year-old with mild cognitive impairment becomes confused weeks after starting oxybutynin. Best change?
why_correct: Oxybutynin has the highest CNS anticholinergic burden; mirabegron relaxes the detrusor via beta3 with no anticholinergic activity.
discriminator: Review all anticholinergics (diphenhydramine, TCAs).

B.why: Oxybutynin has the highest CNS anticholinergic burden; mirabegron relaxes the detrusor via beta3 with no anticholinergic activity.

stem: A 54-year-old with an intact uterus starts estradiol for vasomotor symptoms. What else is required?
why_correct: Unopposed estrogen with a uterus drives endometrial proliferation → hyperplasia and cancer; a progestin counters it.
discriminator: After hysterectomy, estrogen alone is fine.

C.why: Unopposed estrogen with a uterus drives endometrial proliferation → hyperplasia and cancer; a progestin counters it.

stem: A woman on a combined pill starts rifampin for latent TB. What counseling is needed?

distractors.text: Switch rifampin to St. John’s wort

why_correct: Enzyme inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John’s wort) lower combined contraceptive efficacy.
discriminator: Textbook: rifampin speeds estrogen/progestin metabolism.

A.text: Switch rifampin to St. John’s wort

D.why: Enzyme inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John’s wort) lower combined contraceptive efficacy.

stem: Which adverse-effect cluster follows from antimuscarinic OAB therapy?
why_correct: Systemic muscarinic blockade causes dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision and confusion; avoid in narrow-angle glaucoma and retention.
takeaway: Can’t see, can’t spit, can’t poop, can’t think.
discriminator: Burden is cumulative across all drugs.

C.why: Systemic muscarinic blockade causes dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision and confusion; avoid in narrow-angle glaucoma and retention.

stem: Which pairing of drug and mechanism is correct?
why_correct: Mirabegron beta3; oxybutynin M3 (and M2) antagonist; tamsulosin alpha1; finasteride 5-ARI; sildenafil PDE5.
takeaway: One receptor, one location, one class.
discriminator: Metformin in PCOS works through insulin.

E.why: Mirabegron beta3; oxybutynin M3 (and M2) antagonist; tamsulosin alpha1; finasteride 5-ARI; sildenafil PDE5.

stem: A 25-year-old with PCOS, irregular cycles and hirsutism (BMI 32) does not want pregnancy. Best plan?
why_correct: Contraception for immediate symptom control; metformin for the metabolic driver and long-term diabetes risk.
discriminator: GLP-1 agonists: off-label with obesity.

B.why: Contraception for immediate symptom control; metformin for the metabolic driver and long-term diabetes risk.

stem: A man on testosterone injections has a hematocrit of 56%. What is the issue?
why_correct: Testosterone causes erythrocytosis; monitor hematocrit and PSA; oral forms risk hepatotoxicity; suppresses fertility.
discriminator: Contraindicated in prostate cancer and pregnancy.

A.why: Testosterone causes erythrocytosis; monitor hematocrit and PSA; oral forms risk hepatotoxicity; suppresses fertility.

stem: Which receptor–location pair drives voiding?
why_correct: Parasympathetic ACh at M3 contracts the detrusor; sympathetic alpha1 closes the neck and beta3 relaxes the detrusor during storage.
discriminator: M2 is abundant but contributes less.
src: L12 S5; S7; S9; SG U6-R11

A.why: Parasympathetic ACh at M3 contracts the detrusor; sympathetic alpha1 closes the neck and beta3 relaxes the detrusor during storage.

stem: Which drug interaction blunts tamoxifen’s activation?
why_correct: CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine) blunt tamoxifen activation.
discriminator: Tamoxifen also raises INR with warfarin.

B.why: CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine) blunt tamoxifen activation.

stem: A 66-year-old on isosorbide mononitrate for angina requests tadalafil. What should the PA do?
why_correct: Nitrates and PDE5 inhibitors both raise NO/cGMP; together, life-threatening hypotension — an absolute contraindication.
discriminator: Riociguat is also contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors.

C.why: Nitrates and PDE5 inhibitors both raise NO/cGMP; together, life-threatening hypotension — an absolute contraindication.

stem: A man on dutasteride for 2 years has a PSA of 2.1 ng/mL. How should it be interpreted?
why_correct: 5-ARIs lower PSA by roughly half on long-term therapy; adjust when interpreting.
discriminator: Onset of benefit 3–6 months.

E.why: 5-ARIs lower PSA by roughly half on long-term therapy; adjust when interpreting.

stem: How do estrogens produce their effects on the endometrium, bone and lipids?
why_correct: Estrogens bind intracellular ER-alpha/ER-beta and regulate gene transcription in reproductive, bone, cardiovascular and CNS tissue.
discriminator: Effects: endometrial proliferation, bone density, ↑ HDL ↓ LDL.

E.why: Estrogens bind intracellular ER-alpha/ER-beta and regulate gene transcription in reproductive, bone, cardiovascular and CNS tissue.

stem: A 38-year-old who smokes daily asks for contraception. Which choice is most appropriate?

distractors.text: Combined pill at the lowest dose

why_correct: Smoking with age over 35 substantially raises estrogen’s thromboembolic risk; progestin-only methods carry no estrogen.
takeaway: Smoker > 35, VTE history, migraine with aura → progestin-only.
discriminator: When estrogen is off the table, progestin-only is the right first choice.

B.text: Combined pill at the lowest dose

C.why: Smoking with age over 35 substantially raises estrogen’s thromboembolic risk; progestin-only methods carry no estrogen.

stem: How do bicalutamide and finasteride differ in reducing androgen action?
why_correct: Flutamide/bicalutamide are direct AR blockers (prostate cancer, with a GnRH agonist); finasteride/dutasteride block testosterone → DHT.
discriminator: Same drugs (5-ARIs) return for BPH.

E.why: Flutamide/bicalutamide are direct AR blockers (prostate cancer, with a GnRH agonist); finasteride/dutasteride block testosterone → DHT.

stem: A patient with poorly controlled hypertension needs OAB therapy. What is the concern with mirabegron?
why_correct: Mirabegron can raise blood pressure — monitor in uncontrolled hypertension; it also inhibits CYP2D6.
takeaway: Mirabegron: no anticholinergic burden, but watch BP.
discriminator: Can combine with an antimuscarinic for refractory OAB.

D.why: Mirabegron can raise blood pressure — monitor in uncontrolled hypertension; it also inhibits CYP2D6.

stem: A 42-year-old premenopausal woman with ER-positive breast cancer asks about letrozole alone. Best answer?

distractors.text: It raises estrogen to fight tumor

why_correct: Aromatase inhibitors block peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogen; before menopause the ovary dominates (needs ovarian suppression).
discriminator: Protect bone: calcium, vitamin D, bisphosphonate.

B.text: It raises estrogen to fight tumor

C.why: Aromatase inhibitors block peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogen; before menopause the ovary dominates (needs ovarian suppression).

stem: Why is metformin called an indirect therapy for hyperandrogenism in PCOS?
correct: It lowers insulin, so androgens fall
why_correct: Metformin improves insulin sensitivity and reduces hyperinsulinemia’s stimulation of ovarian androgens — no hormone receptor involved.
discriminator: GI upset; hold for contrast or renal impairment.

A.text: It lowers insulin, so androgens fall
A.why: Metformin improves insulin sensitivity and reduces hyperinsulinemia’s stimulation of ovarian androgens — no hormone receptor involved.

stem: A man with BPH wants quick relief and a smaller prostate long term. Best regimen?
why_correct: Alpha1 blockers act in days; 5-ARIs shrink the prostate over 3–6 months — frequently combined.
discriminator: 5-ARI: PSA halved; pregnant partners avoid crushed tablets.

A.why: Alpha1 blockers act in days; 5-ARIs shrink the prostate over 3–6 months — frequently combined.

stem: While counseling a patient, you learn his wife has new vaginal bleeding on tamoxifen. What do you advise?
why_correct: Tamoxifen’s endometrial agonism raises hyperplasia/cancer risk; new bleeding warrants prompt evaluation.
discriminator: The U6 integrated case pulls Session 1 into Session 2.

D.why: Tamoxifen’s endometrial agonism raises hyperplasia/cancer risk; new bleeding warrants prompt evaluation.

stem: During storage, what does norepinephrine do at alpha1 and beta3 receptors?

distractors.text: Contracts the detrusor and opens the neck

why_correct: Alpha1 at the bladder neck contracts (continence); beta3 on the detrusor relaxes (low-pressure filling).
takeaway: Alpha1 = door shut; beta3 = tank relaxed.
discriminator: Both become drug targets: tamsulosin and mirabegron.

B.why: Alpha1 at the bladder neck contracts (continence); beta3 on the detrusor relaxes (low-pressure filling).

E.text: Contracts the detrusor and opens the neck

stem: A man on tamsulosin (no nitrates) wants sildenafil. What is the remaining concern?
why_correct: Alpha1 blockade and NO-cGMP potentiation both lower BP — less severe than nitrates but warrants spacing or monitoring.
discriminator: Tadalafil profile allows tamsulosin 0.4 mg with caution.

B.why: Alpha1 blockade and NO-cGMP potentiation both lower BP — less severe than nitrates but warrants spacing or monitoring.

stem: Why do alpha1 blockers for BPH cause orthostatic hypotension?

distractors.text: They act only in the bladder

why_correct: Alpha1 blockade at the bladder neck also lowers systemic vascular resistance — orthostasis and a first-dose effect.
takeaway: Same receptor family as the Unit 5 antihypertensives.
discriminator: Give the first dose of doxazosin at bedtime.

B.text: They act only in the bladder

C.why: Alpha1 blockade at the bladder neck also lowers systemic vascular resistance — orthostasis and a first-dose effect.

stem: How do PDE5 inhibitors produce an erection?

distractors.text: They block alpha1 in the penis

why_correct: NANC nerves release NO → cGMP → smooth-muscle relaxation; PDE5 inhibitors prolong cGMP.
takeaway: No stimulation, no signal to prolong.
discriminator: Tadalafil has the longest half-life.

C.text: They block alpha1 in the penis

D.why: NANC nerves release NO → cGMP → smooth-muscle relaxation; PDE5 inhibitors prolong cGMP.
